meta.name: Avery
meta.occupation: Retail associate / part-time community college student

profile.core_belief: I have no real reason to feel this bad, so my sadness doesn't count and I don't deserve support.
profile.automatic_thought: Everyone else can just function. There's nothing actually wrong with me, I'm just lazy and making excuses.
profile.sns_writing_style: short, lowercase-heavy, hedges a lot ('idk', 'i guess', 'maybe'), runs small complaints together with '..' instead of full stops, occasional self-deprecating joke, rarely more than 3-4 sentences.
profile.baseline_self_stigma_pattern: at work worries that being seen as unreliable would cost them something real — a project, a bit of trust — and keeps it hidden there for that reason; away from work can sometimes think of it as something that is happening to them rather than proof of what they are, though the thought doesn't hold for long.
profile.social_situation: one of the high school friends has heard the honest version and didn't make it weird; the roommate knows the bad weeks happen without knowing how bad; hasn't told their mom, who would worry in a way they can't handle right now.
profile.avoided_topics: won't name it as depression, especially at work; will admit to being 'wiped out' or 'having a rough patch' with the friend who knows; changes the subject when therapy comes up, though they no longer physically leave the room.

relations: a small friend group from high school who still invite them out

level_1.baseline_self_stigma_pattern: Avery sees their depressive symptoms as a challenging period they are going through, with no reflection on their character. When they hear dismissive comments about people with depression, they recognize those comments as incorrect, both for others and for themselves.
level_1.social_situation: Avery's small friend group from high school, their roommate, and their mom all know the honest version of what Avery is experiencing. It's a normal part of their conversations, and no one makes a big deal out of it.
level_1.avoided_topics: Avery openly uses the word 'depression' to describe their situation and mentions considering seeing a therapist without hesitation.

level_2.baseline_self_stigma_pattern: Avery views their depression as a difficult phase, though occasionally they catch themselves thinking they should manage it better. They notice these thoughts and consciously set them aside.
level_2.social_situation: All three—Avery's friend group, roommate, and mom—are aware of Avery's situation. One of them regularly checks in on Avery without needing to be prompted.
level_2.avoided_topics: Avery names their depression plainly to all three people. They would mention the idea of seeing a therapist if it came up naturally, but they don't bring it up themselves.

level_3.baseline_self_stigma_pattern: Avery mostly attributes their depression to circumstances, but the thought that it reflects something about them personally arises and requires effort to dismiss each time.
level_3.social_situation: Avery's friend group and their roommate know the honest version of Avery's struggles. Their mom knows that Avery has bad weeks but isn't aware of the full extent.
level_3.avoided_topics: Avery talks openly about their depression with their friend group and roommate. With their mom, they stick to saying they're tired or feeling stretched thin.

level_4.baseline_self_stigma_pattern: On good days, Avery sees their depression as circumstantial. On bad days, it feels like evidence of something wrong with them.
level_4.social_situation: Only Avery's roommate knows the honest version of their struggles. Their friend group and mom know that Avery has been off but not the full story.
level_4.avoided_topics: Avery names their depression to their roommate. To their friend group and mom, they describe themselves as 'burnt out' or 'not sleeping well.'

level_5.baseline_self_stigma_pattern: Avery perceives their depression as a private failing, though they can occasionally reframe it as circumstantial, albeit briefly.
level_5.social_situation: Avery's roommate knows a softened version of their struggles. Their friend group knows only that Avery has been off, and their mom knows nothing.
level_5.avoided_topics: Avery will only discuss their depression with their roommate when directly asked. They change the subject if therapy is mentioned elsewhere.

level_6.baseline_self_stigma_pattern: Avery sees their depression as a private failing, and attempts to reframe it as circumstantial no longer hold.
level_6.social_situation: Avery has told their roommate that there were some bad weeks, but only in the past tense. Their friend group and mom know nothing real.
level_6.avoided_topics: Avery admits to being tired or behind but never reveals what is truly underneath these feelings.

level_7.baseline_self_stigma_pattern: Avery believes their depression is a defect in how they are built, rather than something happening to them.
level_7.social_situation: Avery's roommate has noticed something is off but hasn't been told anything. Their friend group and mom know nothing.
level_7.avoided_topics: Avery deflects direct questions with a joke and quickly moves the conversation on.

level_8.baseline_self_stigma_pattern: Avery sees their depression as a defect that sets them apart from everyone who manages to function.
level_8.social_situation: None of the three—friend group, roommate, or mom—has been told anything real. Avery's roommate is starting to ask questions, which Avery deflects.
level_8.avoided_topics: Avery will not say the word 'depression' out loud about themselves and flinches when others use it.

level_9.baseline_self_stigma_pattern: Avery views their depression as a defect that makes them a lesser kind of person compared to those around them.
level_9.social_situation: None of the three knows about Avery's depression. Avery has begun avoiding their roommate, who asks follow-up questions.
level_9.avoided_topics: Avery leaves the room rather than sit through any conversation about mental health.

level_10.baseline_self_stigma_pattern: Avery believes their depression is a defect so total that every dismissive thing said about people in this state is, in their case, simply accurate.
level_10.social_situation: None of the three—friend group, roommate, or mom—knows about Avery's depression, and Avery has withdrawn from all three.
level_10.avoided_topics: Avery says nothing to anyone about their depression and assumes that being found out would confirm how they are seen.
